reviews.rationale: Sequential comparison of selected SEC exhibit rows shows net interest income after the tax-equivalent adjustment rising while total fees and commissions also rose, with the interest-expense line declining and interest revenue roughly flat, so the net interest income movement is arithmetically consistent with a lower funding-cost line rather than with revenue growth. Average earning assets declined over the same sequential interval, which means the net interest income improvement occurred against a smaller average balance sheet and cannot be read as volume-driven expansion. The tax-equivalent adjustment is a bridge item between tax-equivalent and after-adjustment bases and is not an economic driver. The selected rows contain no net interest margin, yield, rate, mix, provision, credit, capital, or non-GAAP reconciliation detail, and no guidance or realized-vs-guided comparison, so the improvement cannot be attributed to pricing, deposit mix, or balance-sheet composition, and no year-over-year or consensus comparison is supported. Because the evidence is a narrow set of displayed rows rather than complete filings, the absence of these items in the extract is not evidence of their absence from the filings. The thesis remains active at unchanged conviction with the research state maintained; the next earnings release is the natural reassessment point.
